chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Allan, who said: Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār narrated to me, who said: I asked Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about the two rak'ahs that are before Fajr.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Before Fajr, with it, and after it.' I said: 'Then when do I leave them in order to make them up?' He said: 'When the Mu'adhdhin says: The prayer has been established.'

key_terms.أَقْضِيَهَا: Make them up / compensate for them
key_terms.قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ: The prayer has been established (phrase in Adhan)

ai.seo_question: When should the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr be performed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the flexibility of the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr, permitting them before, during, or after the obligatory prayer. He specifies that if one delays them, they should be left once the Mu'adhdhin announces 'Qad Qamat as-Salah' (the prayer is ready), marking the transition from the time of the Sunnah to the onset of the Fard. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of the Fajr Sunnah, which is uniquely tied to the specific moment of the Adhan's conclusion rather than the entire prayer duration.
